page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this instance in the lower tiers of performance. The Intel Xeon 8163 CPU achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1103.19 and a multi-core score of 2934.5, both categorized in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only cached small block speed of 164.06 GB/sec, but uncached large block read performance drops to 20.58 GB/sec, which is in the bottom 10%. Cryptographic and compression tasks also show lower-tier throughput, with single-threaded gzip compression at 19.02 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 7.4 GB/sec.

The ecs.c5.xlarge offers dedicated CPU allocation, ensuring consistent compute resources without virtualization steal, which represents a stable hardware profile for its class. However, the lack of local storage and lower benchmark scores relative to newer architectures present a clear tradeoff. It is best suited for lightweight compute tasks, basic web serving (measured at 3.36 GB/sec static throughput), Redis key-value operations (achieving 2.86 million SET operations per second), and small-scale language model inference.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 physical cores running at 2.5 GHz and 8.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark data places its processing and memory performance in the lower percentiles, with a Geekbench single-core score of 987.0 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 20.58 GB/sec. Despite these lower-tier benchmark results, the dedicated CPU allocation provides stable, non-shared compute resources. This instance is suitable for entry-level compute workloads, lightweight static web serving, Redis caching, and small-scale utility processing.
